sections.html:
Darien's North Way holds both tax offices. The assessors at number 601 appraise property and approve exemptions. At number 1200, in the county annex, the Tax Commissioner prints and mails statements and takes in what owners pay. The commissioner sets neither value nor millage.

McIntosh County numbers worth keeping by the phone
OfficeWhere or whyPhone
Tax Assessor601 North Way, weekdays 8:00 to 4:30912-437-6663
Tax Commissioner1200 North Way, weekdays, same hours912-437-6627
County Commission OfficeBudget and millage912-437-6671
Building and ZoningPermits, flood zone lookups912-437-6603
Superior CourtDeed recording and liens912-437-6641

A house inside Darien may carry a city levy as well. State guidance gives billing of city tax to the city clerk, unless city and county agreed to merge the statements, so City Hall can tell you which applies.

Marsh, tidal rivers and barrier islands define this county, which covers 574 square miles, 150 of them water. Darien is the seat, and Crescent and Eulonia are the other named communities. The population was 11,989 in July 2025, up 9.3 percent from 10,970 in 2020.

Owners hold 80.0 percent of households, in homes worth $182,700 in the middle, and a typical rental costs $800 a month. Builders were issued 106 permits in 2025.

Low coastal plains leave parts of McIntosh County and Darien open to river, canal and hurricane flooding. Lenders ask about flood zones, so look yours up before listing.

Both the county and Darien participate in the federal flood insurance program. Regular homeowners coverage typically excludes flood, and a structure in a mapped high-hazard area with a federally backed mortgage must carry its own flood policy. Building and Zoning at 912-437-6603 looks up zones and base flood elevations and makes free site visits about flooding and drainage.

  • Under the county's 50 percent rule, repairs or renovations that raise a house's value by more than half require the lowest floor to be raised to at least base flood elevation when it sits below it.
  • In the AE and VE zones the underside of the lowest horizontal beam has to clear base flood elevation by one foot.
  • Suggested protection includes lifting electrical panels, heat pumps, water heaters and fuel tanks.

Call Building and Zoning before any pre-sale renovation, since the work itself can bring the elevation rules into play.

November 15, or 60 days after mailing, is the usual deadline, and unpaid property can be levied upon and sold. The 60 days count from the postmark, and each county may choose its own official date.

Returns go in between January 1 and April 1. Without one, last year's return and value stand. An owner who thinks the value is wrong can file a return with their own estimate of market value, which protects appeal rights if the assessors raise it again.

Mobile homes follow a different clock. A home sitting in McIntosh County on January 1 needs tax and location permit settled by April 1, or the owner faces a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale. To contest a mobile home value you have 45 days to reach the Board of Tax Assessors, and then 21 days from the notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Keep proof of every payment. If a statement never arrives, call the commissioner at 912-437-6627 rather than waiting, because the tax is still owed and the clock keeps running.

Send new mailing addresses to the assessor or commissioner quickly, since notices only go to the address on file.

County millage has stayed flat for years at a stretch. In September 2024 the county commission said it planned to collect 19.38 percent more than the rollback rate, citing pay adjustments, a forecast 10 to 15 percent jump in employee health costs and inflation. A rate above rollback triggers three public hearings under state law.

For the current year, ask the County Commission Office for the county millage, and ask Darien City Hall for the city rate if the house is inside city limits.

The Tax Assessor's Office takes homestead applications, and new homeowners bring the warranty deed. A filing earns the current year's benefit only if it arrives by April 1, even though Georgia takes applications all year. Approval stays on the account until you move, sell or switch types, and a larger local exemption beats the state figure.

The standard exemption is $2,000, and elderly relief applies to incomes of $10,000 or less: up to $10,000 on school tax from age 62 and up to $4,000 on general tax from age 65. A floating exemption suits owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less and replaces other state and county exemptions. A deferral for owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less delays tax until ownership changes or the debt hits 85 percent of value.

  • Qualifying farmland may be taxed on 30 percent of market value rather than 40.
  • Conservation use taxes eligible land on its actual use value.
  • Both programs bind the owner to a 10-year covenant.

A buyer does not inherit your exemption, so expect the new owner to file again after closing. Appeals of a real property value go to the Board of Tax Assessors, with a postmark inside 45 days of the notice's mailing.

sections.h2: What to line up before closing
sections.html:
Request each parcel's exact balance from the Tax Commissioner and ask the Assessor's Office whether a change in value or exemption is pending. Gather the flood zone and permit history before the sign goes up.

Deed recording triggers the state transfer tax: $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents on every additional $100, which the seller owes unless the contract assigns it to the buyer.

At the closing table, settle who covers the current-year bill, whether a lender has been paying from escrow, and when your exemption ends. A cash sale moves faster, but it still needs the tax account clear.

A short checklist helps. Bring the warranty deed, the latest statement from the commissioner and any flood zone or permit paperwork to your first meeting with the closing attorney. If the house sits in Darien, add the city bill to the pile, since the city and the county may bill separately. If a mobile home sits on the land, treat it as its own account with its own April 1 deadline, and confirm both are paid before the day of closing.

faqs.q: What is the McIntosh County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: November 15, or 60 days after mailing. A mobile home is due April 1. Treat the date on your own statement as final.

faqs.q: Which McIntosh County office handles a disagreement over value?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors at 601 North Way, 912-437-6663. The Tax Commissioner, 912-437-6627, sends bills and cannot change a value.

faqs.q: Can flood rules affect a McIntosh County house sale?
faqs.a: They can. A federally backed loan on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires flood insurance, and the county's 50 percent rule may require raising the floor after major renovation.

faqs.q: What if a McIntosh County mobile home tax misses April 1?
faqs.a: Expect a 10 percent penalty, with a possible citation to McIntosh County Magistrate Court or sale of the home.

faqs.q: How does a McIntosh County owner apply for homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office, with the filing in by April 1 for that year. New homeowners bring the warranty deed.
